extracted.intended_audience: state air agencies, regulated sources and their counsel, environmental stakeholders, and EPA rulemaking staff
extracted.subtask_short: SIP approval for engine emissions rule
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and final federal approval (and associated CFR amendments) of a State Implementation Plan (SIP) revision adopting a local rule regulating NOx and VOC emissions from internal combustion engines in the Mojave Desert Air Quality Management District.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with the Clean Air Act and applicable federal regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the CAA, the Administrator is required to approve a SIP submission that complies with the provisions of the Act and applicable federal regulations. 42 U.S.C. 7410(k); 40 CFR 52.02(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPA's role is to approve state choices, provided that they meet the criteria of the CAA. This action 'merely approves state law as meeting Federal requirements and does not impose additional requirements beyond those imposed by state law.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule addresses relevant pollutants/sources (NOx and VOCs from internal combustion engines)
rubrics_metrics.description: The submitted revision concerns emissions of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and oxides of nitrogen (NOX) from internal combustion engines; the rule being incorporated is MDAQMD Rule 1160, 'Internal Combustion Engines.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA proposed to approve this rule because it determined that it complies with the relevant CAA requirements; evaluation focuses on whether the local rule regulates the identified emission sources and meets statutory/regulatory criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution of prior deficiencies (limited disapproval) / terminates sanctions and FIP clocks
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval resolves all deficiencies forming the basis for the September 10, 2021 limited disapproval of the prior version of Rule 1160 and permanently terminates all sanctions clocks and federal implementation plan clocks triggered by that limited disapproval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A SIP revision that cures previously-identified deficiencies should demonstrate that the earlier basis for limited disapproval has been addressed; when successful, sanctions (CAA section 179) and FIP triggers (40 CFR 52.31) are ended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment process and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed action provided a 30-day public comment period; EPA reviewed comments (one anonymous supportive comment and one from MDAQMD) and addressed them in the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments that are supportive or that do not raise issues changing EPA's assessment do not alter approval. EPA must make full text of comments available in the docket and respond in the preamble as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative removals/replacements must not weaken the SIP
rubrics_metrics.description: Removing an obsolete rule (e.g., 1981 SCAQMD Rule 1110) from the SIP is permissible as a 'purely administrative revision' when the rule 'does not establish any currently applicable requirement' or has 'no sources subject to it' and its removal 'would not weaken the SIP in any way or otherwise interfere with any requirements of the CAA.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a rule is a fixed-term demonstration program or otherwise inapplicable, EPA can remove it administratively provided that no substantive obligations on sources are lost; documentation in the staff report and comment supporting administrative revision is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference requirements (1 CFR 51.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 1 CFR 51.5, the EPA is finalizing incorporation by reference of MDAQMD Rule 1160 (amended January 23, 2023) into the CFR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents incorporated by reference must be made available (e.g., via regulations.gov and at EPA regional office) and properly cited in the CFR amendments; the final rule should state where the incorporated materials can be accessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: CFR amendment accuracy (paragraph additions/revisions and cross-references)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory text amendments must correctly add, revise, and delete the appropriate paragraph citations in 40 CFR 52.220 (e.g., adding (c)(121)(i)(G), correcting cross-reference to paragraph (c)(518)(i)(A)(7) instead of (c)(518)(i)(A)(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must correct erroneous cross-references and ensure the CFR reflects the current list of approved/replaced rules, including precise paragraph numbering and citations to avoid ambiguity about which versions are approved or removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket availability and treatment of non-public materials
rubrics_metrics.description: All documents in the docket are listed on regulations.gov; some information (e.g., CBI or copyrighted material) may not be publicly available online and may be available only in hard copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule should identify the docket ID, explain how to access public materials (regulations.gov or contact person), and note that certain materials are restricted from online public posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date specification
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule must specify an effective date for the action (this rule is effective September 29, 2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers should include the effective date in the DATES section; the effective date controls when the SIP approval and any CFR amendments legally take effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of whether the action is a significant regulatory action under Executive Order 12866
rubrics_metrics.description: This action 'Is not a significant regulatory action subject to review by the Office of Management and Budget under Executive Order 12866.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must analyze whether an action meets the EO12866 significance criteria and state that determination in the rule's statutory and executive order reviews section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of other statutory and executive order requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule states applicability (or non-applicability) of various statutes and EOs: not subject to EO14192 (because SIP actions are exempt from EO12866 review), does not impose information collection burden under PRA, certified under Regulatory Flexibility Act as not having significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities, does not contain unfunded mandates, does not have federalism implications (EO13132), is not subject to EO13045, is not a significant regulatory action under EO13211, and is not subject to NTTAA section 12(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must evaluate and declare the applicability of each relevant statute/EO and provide rationale (e.g., SIP approvals are exempt from some reviews; certification under RFA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal implications
rubrics_metrics.description: The SIP is not approved to apply on any Indian reservation land or other area where the EPA or an Indian Tribe has demonstrated Tribal jurisdiction; the rule 'does not have Tribal implications and will not impose substantial direct costs on Tribal governments or preempt Tribal law' as specified by EO13175.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When taking SIP actions, EPA must state whether the action has Tribal implications and, if appropriate, exclude Indian country where Tribe jurisdiction exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional Review Act (CRA) reporting and major rule determination
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is subject to the CRA, and EPA will submit a rule report to each House of Congress and the Comptroller General; the action is 'not a “major rule” as defined by 5 U.S.C. 804(2)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA should determine major-rule status under CRA and file the requisite report; state the determination in the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review timing and finality (CAA section 307(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 307(b)(1) of the CAA, petitions for judicial review of this action must be filed in the appropriate U.S. Court of Appeals by October 27, 2025; filing a petition for reconsideration does not affect finality or extend the judicial review period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rules should include the deadline for judicial review and note that seeking reconsideration does not extend that deadline nor postpone effectiveness of the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amending the Identification of plan-in-part (§ 52.220) to reflect deletions and additions
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule amends § 52.220 by adding and revising specific paragraphs to list deletions (e.g., Rule 1110) and additions/replacements (e.g., Rule 1160 incorporated at (c)(628)(i)(A)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative actions must explicitly edit the CFR plan-identification table to show which previously-approved rules are deleted and where the replacing rules are listed to ensure the CFR accurately identifies the SIP content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement of previously approved rule versions
rubrics_metrics.description: The January 23, 2023 version of Rule 1160 will replace the previously approved version of this rule in the SIP; prior versions (e.g., January 22, 2018) are deleted with replacement language in the CFR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a new submitted rule supplants earlier SIP-approved versions, the final rule should state which versions are removed and where the new version is incorporated by reference.
